issue.title: [Bug][GLM-5.2-W4A8C8][co-located] Stochastic async MTP enters a parser-before periodic raw-token loop
issue.body:
## Why this is a separate report

This is an independent **two-node co-located** reproduction, not P/D disaggregation. It is related to #14463 and #14656, but adds two isolation results that those issue bodies do not contain:

1. the failure reproduces through the vLLM OpenAI-compatible endpoint directly, bypassing the agent harness, LiteLLM, and the API gateway;
2. `return_token_ids=true` proves that the periodic loop already exists in the engine's raw output token IDs before GLM tool parsing.

The symptom eventually becomes repeated or unterminated `tool_calls[].function.arguments`, but the parser is downstream of the first observed corruption in this case.

## Impact

In a production-style agent request, approximately 0.9%-1.0% of default-sampling requests entered a long-running periodic token loop. They continued returning HTTP 200 SSE chunks until a 300-second client protection timeout, with no terminal `finish_reason`, usage chunk, or `[DONE]`. If the incomplete tool call is persisted and sent back in a later turn, downstream JSON parsing reports `Unterminated string` and returns HTTP 400.

## Reproduction statistics

All runs used the same request shape and called the serving endpoint directly:

| Arm | Result |
|---|---:|
| default model sampling, concurrency 4 | 991/1000 completed; 9/1000 timed out at 300 s |
| independent default-sampling repeat, concurrency 4 | 297/300 completed; 3/300 timed out at 300 s |
| `temperature=0`, concurrency 4 | 300/300 completed; 0/300 observed timeouts |

The zero failures in 300 greedy requests are evidence that stochastic sampling is a trigger/risk factor; they are not claimed as proof of a complete fix.

The request did **not** set `tool_choice`, `strict`, or `temperature`. It therefore used auto tool choice and the model's default generation configuration (`temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`).

Non-sensitive request shape:

```text
OpenAI Chat Completions
stream=true
about 50,190 prompt tokens after template application
36 messages
85 function tool schemas
max_completion_tokens=128,000 (an upper bound, not a fixed requested output length)
stream_options.include_usage=true
return_token_ids=true for the evidence run
concurrency=4
per-request protection timeout=300 seconds
```

## Parser-before raw-token evidence

All three failures in the 300-request evidence run had low-diversity periodic repetition in raw `output.token_ids` before parser processing. The three token-stream hashes and best periods were different, so this is not one SSE response duplicated by the client or proxy.

| Request | Raw engine token evidence | Token-stream SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| 44 | best period 13 over the last 8192 tokens; 74.61% agreement | `a5f86d630332741d00746281a50594bd4d07f4496f63f08cd5201c45419a096b` |
| 82 | exact period 768 over a 6144-token tail; 5376/5376 comparable tokens match | `e1df762935c36e64f1383e0bfba62c9f86683e3d27a45d0b8c3a69bd3fee754d` |
| 142 | exact period 8 over the last 8192 tokens; 8184/8184 comparable tokens match | `eb9cd9c12bffa1ebe41dba9c4294bf1c9749082c67494a045314cb9d5cd13b5b` |

After those raw-token loops begin, the parser converts the repeated GLM tool markup into repeated/unclosed arguments. For request 82, the parsed argument tail also repeats exactly (period 1248 characters) and ends with `Unterminated string`. Request 142 independently produces a different repeated argument period and the same incomplete-JSON class.

## Environment

```text
Hardware: two Atlas 800 A3 hosts, 16 Ascend910 devices visible per host
Deployment: co-located serving, not P/D disaggregation
Parallelism: DP4 / TP8 / DCP8 / PCP1 / PP1, EP enabled
Model: GLM-5.2-W4A8C8, GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM
Speculative decode: deepseek_mtp, num_speculative_tokens=3
KV connector: AscendStoreConnector, kv_role=kv_both, MemCache backend
Context: max-model-len=1,024,000
Tool parser: glm47
Reasoning parser: glm45
CANN: 9.1.0, innerversion V100R001C11SPC001B243
PyTorch: 2.10.0+cpu
torch-npu: 2.10.0.post4
vLLM: 0.23.0, commit 0fc695fc6d1d82e9a5ac6835ac8e4e1c83703665
vLLM-Ascend: 0.23.0, commit 5cb98caaadeff42b5b62b996e34bb2aaa29d20fd
transformers: 5.5.4
```

Immutable official base image:

```text
quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend@sha256:382b012420854ba2d8b3b78897d9216742f27948345e503a01644ebbdd706ce6
```

The derivative image, Dockerfile, and applied parser backports are documented here:

https://gist.github.com/ZhengDeL/0b63136e32a5e573109aa4e1afb18d57

Complete sanitized host commands, image provenance, package versions, model fingerprints, and source hashes were already posted here:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/14463#issuecomment-5345634154

## Fix/version audit already performed

- vLLM #45915 and #46351 are present in the tested image. They improve GLM streaming parsing, but the parser-before token loop still reproduces.
- vLLM-Ascend #13865 is present byte-for-byte in both serving images. The issue still reproduces, so the async accepted-token snapshot fix is insufficient by itself.
- vLLM #47512 / issue #47504 cover `tool_choice=required`; this request uses auto tool choice and does not set `tool_choice`.
- vLLM #52805 covers speculative grammar advancement after structural-tag termination. This request has neither `strict` nor required/named tool choice, so it does not build that constrained structural-tag path.
- vLLM-Ascend #13766 fixes an always-accepting rejection sampler in ModelRunner V2 on v0.26+. The tested v0.23 path is ModelRunner V1 and uses generated uniform probabilities, not the hardcoded `u=0.0` code fixed there.
- vLLM-Ascend #14536 is specific to P/D decode nodes with `enable_sparse_sfa_c8`; this reproduction is co-located and uses `enable_sparse_li_c8` without `enable_sparse_sfa_c8`.
- vLLM-Ascend #14451 may be relevant to GLM-5.2 MTP shared-index handling on the v0.26rc line, but it is still a draft with no end-to-end validation for this failure mode.
- As of 2026-08-20, the latest published vLLM-Ascend release is v0.23.0. Main/v0.26rc contains additional candidate fixes, but no released or merged change claims to fix this parser-before periodic raw-token loop.

## Questions for maintainers

1. Which component should own the next isolation step: GLM hybrid/MTP state, DCP/distributed decode state, W4A8C8 numerical behavior, or KV reuse?
2. Is there an exact main/release-branch commit that is expected to fix this raw-token loop, rather than only malformed parser output?
3. Is #14451 applicable to in-model `deepseek_mtp` under this DP4/TP8/DCP8 topology, and if so, which commit should be tested?
4. Could the diagnostic facilities in #12209 (MTP acceptance/token-repeat/logprob/tensor dump) be provided as a testable branch or minimal patch for this case?
5. We can run controlled A/B tests on isolated validation instances with raw token capture: MTP on/off, DCP on/off, async path on/off, MemCache on/off, and W4A8C8 versus W8A8C8/BF16. Please advise the preferred order and any additional tensors/counters to capture.

This is affecting a production tool-calling workload. We would appreciate an owner and priority triage. The customer payload cannot be posted publicly, but a complete evidence archive can be shared privately with maintainers if needed.

issue.title: [Bug]: Vector core exception (errcode 507035) in MoE routing TopK crashes all 16 ranks on Atlas A3 running GLM-5.3-Flash under concurrent long-prompt load
issue.body:
### Your current environment

[vllm-a3-crash_20260907_170631.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31910401/vllm-a3-crash_20260907_170631.log)

- vllm-ascend: quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:glm-5.3-flash-a3
- torch / torch_npu: 2.10.0+cpu / 2.10.0.post2
- CANN: 9.1.0 + a vendor custom-opp package (custom_transformer) providing a high-performance TopKV2 kernel
- Driver / firmware: 25.5.1 (V100R001C23SPC006B220)
- Platform: Atlas A3 super pod node, 16 x Ascend910 (8 chips x 2 dies), TP=16 with EP
- Model: GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8 (public MIT release)

Launch command (paths sanitized):

```bash
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=400
# sources a vendor custom-opp package:
#   /usr/local/Ascend/cann-9.1.0/opp/vendors/custom_transformer/bin/set_env.bash

vllm serve /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 133120 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --quantization ascend \
  --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8,16,32,64,96,128]}'
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The service crashed twice with an identical signature — once after ~16h of uptime and once after
~1.7h after restart — so the failure is uptime-independent and deterministic.

Python-side error (identical in both crashes, in MoE token dispatch preprocess):

```text
File "vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/token_dispatcher.py", line 623, in _preprocess
    global_input_tokens_local_experts_indices = torch.repeat_interleave(
RuntimeError: operator():../torch_npu/csrc/aten/common/LocalScalarDenseNpu.cpp:23 NPU function error:
c10_npu::acl::AclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout(copy_stream), error code is 507035
[ERROR] ERR00100 PTA call acl api failed
[Error]: The vector core execution is abnormal.
```

Device-side error:

```text
The error from device(chipId:x, dieId:y), serial number is 1, there is an exception of fftsplus
aivector error, vec error info: 0x470000020d, subErrType:4, errorStr: The VEC instruction parameter is invalid.
An error occurred in the kernel task, retCode=0x31, [vector core exception]
rtStreamSynchronizeWithTimeout execution failed, reason=vector core exception
```

Key observations:

1. All 16 devices failed in the same second with bit-identical vec error info (0x470000020d).
   npu-smi reports Health OK for every device before and after, and the failing task serial number
   is 1/2 on every device. This looks like a deterministic kernel/tiling bug, not a hardware fault.
2. The device exception dump identifies the failing kernel: the dump directory next to each
   exception_info.* file contains only TopKV2_<hash>_high_performance_*_host.o — i.e. the crashing
   kernel is the custom high-performance TopKV2 from the vendor opp package (MoE routing top-k),
   not repeat_interleave itself; repeat_interleave is only where the stream synchronize surfaced
   the error. The dumps also contain full tiling data (64B) and input tensors.
3. The trigger pattern is reproducible: right before both crashes, a burst of 4 concurrent requests
   with ~32K-token prompts arrived (identical traffic replayed both times: Avg prompt throughput
   3276.7 tokens/s, then Running: 2 reqs, Waiting: 2 reqs), and the crash happened during the first
   mixed chunked-prefill + decode forward passes (max_num_batched_tokens=8192).
4. The crash occurred while the acl-graph wrapper executed the step via its eager fallback
   (acl_graph.py fx_run_eagerly), since the mixed-batch shape is not covered by decode-only graphs.
   Additionally, at startup every worker recorded
   "EE1016: Synchronous memory copy failed ... capture mode GLOBAL(0) ... supported only in
   RELAXED mode" during graph capture — pointing at the same op family (synchronous scalar copy
   inside repeat_interleave) being incompatible with GLOBAL capture.

Current workaround / status:

- Temporarily ran with --enforce-eager and reduced limits (--max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 1):
  service was up, no 507035/EE1016 during that run. However, the original crash happened on the
  eager fallback path, so enforce-eager alone may not fully avoid it.
- Next step we plan to try: drop the custom_transformer vendor opp package from the env so TopK
  falls back to the native implementation, and re-run the trigger traffic.
- npu-smi health is OK; we have per-device exception_info dumps (incl. tiling data) and plog
  available if needed.

Questions:

1. Is this a known issue with the custom high-performance TopKV2 kernel under mixed
   chunked-prefill batches?
2. Is there a supported way to force native TopK for this model (instead of removing the whole
   vendor opp package), e.g. an op-priority config?
3. Any fixed version you can point us to?

issue.title: [Bug]: Long Chinese-context (≈8k+ chars) generation is corrupted for a DeepSeek-V2 model on vLLM-Ascend (works <5k, works on SGLang)
issue.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>The output of `python collect_env.py`</summary>

```text
- Python   : 3.11.15
- torch    : 2.10.0 (torch_npu 2.10.0)
- vLLM     : v0.20.2 (V1 engine)
- vLLM-Ascend : 0.20.2rc1 (register: ascend -> vllm_ascend)
- transformers : 5.5.3
- CANN     : 9.0   (npu-smi 25.5.0)
- NPU      : Ascend 910C (16x, 64GB), TP=2 (逻辑卡 10,11)
- OS       : Linux (manas-npu-node1)
```

</details>


### 🐛 Describe the bug

## 1. Issue summary

For a **DeepSeek-V2** architecture model (custom fine-tuned 32B MoE), chat-completions generation is **corrupted (garbled Chinese, `�` replacement chars, repetition loop, `finish_reason=length`)** whenever the user prompt is **longer than roughly 5k–8k characters** (~2k–8k tokens). Short prompts (<5k chars) generate normally. The corruption is **independent of configuration** (verified below) and **does NOT reproduce on SGLang with the same weights** → it points to a vLLM-Ascend implementation/long-context issue for this model family.

- vLLM-Ascend log maps the `DeepseekV2ForCausalLM` model to `vllm_ascend.models.deepseek_v4:AscendDeepseekV4ForCausalLM` (see log line below). The model's own config says `model_type: deepseek_v2`, `architectures: ["DeepseekV2ForCausalLM"]`.

## 2. Model

- Path: a local `DeepseekV2ForCausalLM` 32B MoE (021-32b fine-tune).
- `config.json`: `model_type` = `deepseek_v2`, `architectures` = `["DeepseekV2ForCausalLM"]`,
  `max_position_embeddings=32768`, `rope_theta=1e6`,
  `rope_scaling={"type":"yarn","factor":1.0,"original_max_position_embeddings":32768,"beta_fast":32,"beta_slow":1,"mscale":1,"mscale_all_dim":1}`.
- Tokenizer: `trust_remote_code` with a custom `MixedTokenizer` (per-base DNA tokens `<d_>_X`, byte-level). Chinese/English encode correctly after tokenizer fixes (prompt token counts are correct: 15.5k chars → 11116 tokens).

## 3. Reproduction

### 3.1 Startup command

```bash
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model /path/to/model \
  --served-model-name 021-32b-best --port 30001 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --distributed_executor_backend mp --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_r1 \
  --block-size 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --async-scheduling \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --compilation_config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8,16,24,32]}' \
  --hf-overrides '{"max_position_embeddings":131072,"rope_parameters":{"rope_type":"yarn","factor":1.0,"original_max_position_embeddings":131072,"beta_fast":32.0,"beta_slow":1.0,"mscale":1.0,"mscale_all_dim":1.0}}'
```

Startup log shows the architecture mapping:

```
WARNING registry.py:945 Model architecture DeepseekV4ForCausalLM is already registered,
and will be overwritten by the new model class vllm_ascend.models.deepseek_v4:AscendDeepseekV4ForCausalLM.
```

### 3.2 Request

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:30001/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
    "model": "021-32b-best",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "<long Chinese prompt ~14k–20k chars; e.g. a structured clinical-analysis instruction with patient data>"}],
    "max_tokens": 8192, "temperature": 0.0
  }'
```

> The full prompt is a Chinese-language structured task (~14k chars). 

### 3.3 Actual (broken)

```text
finish_reason = length
content       = null (empty)
reasoning     = ~13k chars, from the very first token it is garbled Chinese/ASCII mix
                with many U+FFFD replacement chars and repeated fragments, e.g.:
  '###（HAG-PS：.\n（A-1”。\n-    1，"（Hun-1”（B- 该（S-    1”：\n" ... � ... \n###\n###\n###...'
No usable JSON/answer is produced.
```

> **Byte-level clarification:** this is genuine garbage **produced by the model's byte stream**, not a display/decoder issue.
> The `U+FFFD` replacement chars can only arise from invalid UTF-8 byte sequences reaching the detokenizer; short Chinese outputs on the same server decode cleanly (0 `U+FFFD`), so the ByteLevel decoder itself is fine — the corruption is specifically in the long-context generated token/byte stream.

### 3.4 Expected

```text
Model should produce a coherent Chinese chain-of-thought and a final answer (JSON).
Same weights + same prompt on SGLang 0.5.17.dev386 (deepseek-r1 parser) → works: coherent Chinese reasoning, JSON answer, finish_reason=stop.
```

## 4. Length threshold (the key signal)

Same prompt truncated to different lengths (`max_tokens=4096–8192`, temp=0):

| Input length (chars) | Output |
| --- | --- |
| ~2,000 | OK (finish=stop, no U+FFFD) |
| ~5,000 | OK (finish=stop, no U+FFFD) |
| ~8,000 | **BROKEN** (finish=length, reasoning ~9.8k chars, U+FFFD, repetition) |
| ~14,000+ | **BROKEN** (finish=length, reasoning ~13k chars, U+FFFD from first token) |

Short tasks on the same server are fine (e.g., Chinese arithmetic answers correctly), so it is specifically a **long-context** problem, not a general/Chinese/tokenizer problem.

## 5. A/B already tested (all still reproduce ⇒ config-independent)

| Attempt | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` (chunked prefill) | still BROKEN |
| MC2 off (`VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FUSED_MC2=0`) + no `--enable-expert-parallel` | still BROKEN |
| `--enforce-eager` (no OOT compile / no CUDAGraph) | still BROKEN |
| RoPE `--hf-overrides factor=4.0` vs `1.0` | both BROKEN |
| `/no_think` (system msg) or `enable_thinking=false` | still BROKEN (long); helps only short tasks |
| `repetition_penalty=1.05 / 1.1` | still BROKEN (so not a plain repetition that sampling can fix) |
| SGLang (same weights, `--reasoning-parser deepseek-r1`) | **works** (coherent, JSON, stop) |

## 6. Supporting observations

- The corrupted output starts garbled at the **first generated token** for long prompts → the encoded context itself appears corrupted before/at prefill-decode transition, not a mid-roll divergence.
- `enable_chunked_prefill=True`, `compile_ranges_endpoints=[2048]` (from log).
- Possible related upstream issues (same family, DeepSeek + long-context/repeat on vLLM-Ascend):
  - #13661 `dsv4f0731 will repeat and repeat hungup`
  - #14118 `Prompt corruption/leak under high concurrency with prefix caching enabled for DeepSeek-...`
  - #9983 `Disable fused MC2 ... to prevent logit corruption`
  - #5823 (closed) `mla_v1.py ... strongly bound to deepseek_yarn rope_type` — DeepSeek MLA rope is custom on Ascend
  - #12723 / #12820 — examples of Ascend rope silently corrupting positions / QK

## 7. Ask

1. Why does the model register as `AscendDeepseekV4ForCausalLM` although `config.architectures` is `DeepseekV2ForCausalLM`? Could the DeepSeek-V2 → DeepSeek-V4 code path mishandle long-context MLA/rope for this model?
2. Any fix/workaround for long-context (>8k chars) correctness on vLLM-Ascend for DeepSeek-V2 models?

issue.title: [Performance]: Qwen3-235B accuracy and performance issues on releases/v0.26.0rc
issue.body:
## Model
Qwen3-235B-A22B-w8a8-rot and Qwen3-235B W4A8 (800IA3)

## Issue
On `releases/v0.26.0rc`, some PD separation and PD disaggregation tests show lower accuracy or performance than the baseline.

For the A3 single-machine aclgraph case (`32768_4096_TPOT50ms`), the measured TPOT values are `258.2517, 260.6926, 263.8598, 255.5208`, compared with the baseline `273.432`.

This issue will be tracked in the follow-up sunset plan.
